practice.title: Practice
practice.lead: Between design and delivery: drawings, permits, schedules and site safety.
paragraphs: I trained as an architect and have six years of practice in the field, moving from producing construction documents to leading projects and running site supervision. Most of that work was residential, interior and hospitality: the kind of project where the drawings have to survive contact with a real contractor on a real site.

Wanting to oversee how designs physically get built, I moved to the United States to study project management, with a concentration in construction management, at Northeastern University, where my coursework has included a baseline planning model for a regional transit project and a community-focused capstone. At Quantum Design & Safety in New York I designed three accessory dwelling units for the city’s pre-approved plan library, produced the full interior drawing set for a single-family house upstate, ran zoning feasibility studies, worked through DOB permitting, drafted Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans and built construction schedules in Primavera P6. I also coordinated site-specific safety plans and egress drawings for city construction projects, this time under the New York City Department of Buildings rather than RAJUK.

Alongside the design work I ran operations for the firm’s site safety school, 1A Accredited Bilingual Safety Training, a DOB-approved SST course provider: scheduling classes, issuing worker and supervisor cards, building interactive SCORM-compliant training modules in Articulate Storyline 360, and growing sales by 36%.

I draw in AutoCAD, Revit, SketchUp and Rhino, render in Enscape, Lumion and V-Ray, schedule in Primavera P6 and Microsoft Project, build training content in Articulate Storyline 360 and edit video in Wondershare Filmora. I also work with AI tools including Claude, Gemini and GPT models, and I pick up new software quickly. I speak English and Bengali fluently and conversational Hindi.
